{{nihongo|'''Hirose Shrine'''|広瀬神社 (三島市)}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located within {{ill|Rakuju-en|arz|راكوجو اون|ja|楽寿園|qid=Q11541603}} in {{ill|Mishima, Shizuoka|ar|ميشيما (شيزوكا)|arz|ميشيما, شيزوكا|az|Mişima (şəhər)|azb|میشیما، شیزوئوکا|ce|Мисима (гӀала)|ceb|Mishima (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Mišima (Šizuoka)|de|Mishima (Shizuoka)|eo|Miŝima (Ŝizuoka)|es|Mishima (Shizuoka)|et|Mishima|fa|میشیما، شیزوئوکا|fi|Mishima (Shizuoka)|fr|Mishima (Shizuoka)|gl|Mishima, Shizuoka|hy|Միսիմա|id|Mishima, Shizuoka|it|Mishima (Shizuoka)|ja|三島市|ko|미시마시|mzn|میشیما، شیزوئوکا|nl|Mishima (Shizuoka)|no|Mishima|pl|Mishima (miasto)|pt|Mishima|ro|Mishima, Shizuoka|ru|Мисима (город)|sh|Mishima, Shizuoka|simple|Mishima, Shizuoka|sr|Мишима|sv|Mishima, Shizuoka|tg|Мишима|th|มิชิมะ|tl|Mishima|tr|Mishima, Şizuoka|tt|Мисима (шәһәр)|uk|Місіма (Сідзуока)|ur|میشیما، شیزوکا|vi|Mishima, Shizuoka|war|Mishima, Shizuoka|zh|三島市|zh_classical|三島市|zh_min_nan|Misima-chhī|zh_yue|三島|qid=Q653478}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. {{nihongo|'''Hirose Shrine'''|広瀬神社 (三島市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

== Overview ==
The shrine is situated just south of {{ill|Mishima Station|arz|محطة ميشيما|de|Bahnhof Mishima|eo|Stacio Mishima|fr|Gare de Mishima|id|Stasiun Mishima|it|Stazione di Mishima|ja|三島駅|ko|미시마역|ru|Мисима (станция)|su|Stasion Mishima|ur|میشیما اسٹیشن|zh|三島站|qid=Q375061}}, in the southern part of {{ill|Rakuju-en|arz|راكوجو اون|ja|楽寿園|qid=Q11541603}}. It stands in the eastern section of “Miyajima,” a small island in Kohama Pond (Kohama-ike), where a small sanctuary was rebuilt and enshrined.

Hirose Shrine is considered a disputed candidate for a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and it is also identified with “Jūichii Hirose Myōjin” listed in the {{ill|Izu no Kuni Shinkaichō|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}}. However, it is often explained that when {{ill|Mishima Taisha|el|Μισίμα Τάισα|fr|Mishima-taisha|ja|三嶋大社|tr|Mishima Tapınağı|zh|三嶋大社|qid=Q650772}} was relocated northward to its current site, coinciding with the transfer of the provincial capital in ancient times, this shrine was founded as a branch shrine and distant worship site of {{ill|Hirose Shrine (Izunokuni)|ja|広瀬神社 (伊豆の国市)|qid=Q111776816|lt=Hirose Shrine}} located in present-day {{ill|Izunokuni|ar|إزونوكني (شيزوكا)|arz|ازونوكنى|azb|ایزونوکونی، شیزوئوکا|ce|Идзунокуни|ceb|Izunokuni (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Izunokuni|es|Izunokuni (Shizuoka)|et|Izunokuni|fa|ایزونوکونی، شیزوئوکا|fi|Izunokuni|fr|Izunokuni|gl|Izunokuni|id|Izunokuni, Shizuoka|it|Izunokuni|ja|伊豆の国市|ko|이즈노쿠니시|mzn|ایزونوکونی، شیزوئوکا|nl|Izunokuni|pl|Izunokuni|pt|Izunokuni|ro|Izunokuni|ru|Идзунокуни|sv|Izunokuni|tg|Изунокуни|tl|Izunokuni|tr|İzunokuni|tt|Идзунокуни|tum|Izunokuni|uk|Ідзунокуні|vi|Izunokuni, Shizuoka|war|Izunokuni, Shizuoka|zh|伊豆之國市|zh_classical|伊豆之國市|zh_min_nan|Izunokuni-chhī|zh_yue|伊豆之國|qid=Q863758}} ({{ill|Ōhito, Shizuoka|fa|اوهیتو، شیزوئوکا|ja|大仁町|ko|오히토정|ur|اوہٹو، شیزوکا|qid=Q8081497|lt=Ohito}})<ref name="sh">[https://shrineheritager.com/hirose-shrine/amp/ Hirose Shrine] - Shrine Heritager</ref><ref name="engi">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140210-02.html Hirose Shrine] - Research on Engishiki Shrines</ref>.

The area where Rakujuen and Mishima Station now stand was formerly a shrine-and-temple precinct known as Kohamayama. Along with Aizen-in (now defunct) and {{ill|Sengen Shrine (Izu Province Ni-no-Miya)|Q30925511|qid=Q30925511|lt=Asama Shrine}} (the Sannomiya of Izu Province, later Nomiya), it was enshrined there as the Shinomiya of Izu Province, and it was formerly a {{ill|Sessha|Q135009904|qid=Q135009904}} of Mishima Taisha<ref name="sh"/><ref name="engi"/>.

Amid surrounding development after the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, including the construction of a Komatsunomiya imperial villa on the present site of Rakujuen in Meiji 23 ({{ill|1890|Q7832|qid=Q7832}}), the shrine was temporarily relocated to the adjacent precinct of Asama Shrine. Later, in Shōwa 27 ({{ill|1952|Q5272|qid=Q5272}}), when Rakujuen became a public park, the shrine was rebuilt within the park<ref name="sh"/>.
